title: How drinking too much water swells your brain 💧
subject: water
description:
How much water do you drink on a long run? 👇

Water intoxication (hyponatremia) happens when you drink faster than your body can get rid of water: blood sodium drops, cells swell, and the brain has no room to expand. A study of 488 Boston Marathon runners found 13 percent had it.

Sources: Almond et al., "Hyponatremia among Runners in the Boston Marathon", New England Journal of Medicine (2005); American Medical Society for Sports Medicine press release (2005); The Harvard Crimson, "Too Much Water Found Harmful" (18 Apr 2005)

scenes.text: You can drink so much water that your brain swells.
Drink faster than your body can get rid of it, and your blood sodium gets diluted.
Water floods into your cells and they swell. In your brain, the skull leaves almost no room.
In 2002, doctors tested 488 Boston Marathon runners.
13 percent finished with low blood sodium. 3 were critical.
The New England Journal of Medicine study found the ones at risk gained weight during the race. They drank more than they sweated.
